minutes.headline: Conservation Commission approved two projects with conditions, continued four hearings, and approved a $1,500 wetlands peer review.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Conservation Commission met by Zoom and heard several notice of intent and request for determination hearings. Orders of conditions were voted for 1201 Mass Ave and 97 Cross Street; the 154 Peninsula Drive project was moved with conditions, and several hearings were continued to June 5 or June 19. The commission also approved a peer review quote, closed a violation at 141 Hemlock Drive, and approved a certificate of compliance.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission issued orders of conditions for a duplex at 1201 Mass Ave and for 97 Cross Street, the latter pending a Natural Heritage email.
The commission approved the 154 Peninsula Drive project with conditions on plantings and timing; one member was recused.
Hearings for Crossroad Lot 2, PJ Keating and 255 Sunny Hill Road were continued to June 5, and 171 Arbor Street and 390 Howard Street to June 19.
The commission accepted the Goddard quote for a wetlands peer review at 255 Sunny Hill Road, after an earlier vote named the wrong company.
The commission closed the violation notice at 141 Hemlock Drive and approved a certificate of compliance for 190 Electric Ave.

why_it_matters: Conservation Commission conditions decide what can be built near wetlands, so these orders set limits on building at the named properties, including work timing, plantings and erosion control.
A peer review of a wetlands delineation is a cost attached to an application, and a vote to fund beaver deceivers at the Quarry is expected at a later meeting.
watch_next: Continued hearings resume June 5 (Crossroad Lot 2, PJ Keating, 255 Sunny Hill Road, Lancaster Ave determinations) and June 19 (171 Arbor Street, 390 Howard Street).
A vote on money for beaver deceivers at the Quarry is expected at a later meeting.

Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on all eleven non-procedural votes, with outcomes and continuation dates matching, and the differences are mostly caption errors in names and addresses. The one substantive difference is 141 Hemlock Drive: ours says an October 2021 extension lets the applicant proceed, while the official records a condition to finish before October and call for a site visit.
